incidents.name: OneRing vault share pricing manipulation
incidents.notes: The OneRing vault derived its share price from the live state of the underlying stablecoin pools, so a flash-loaned USDC deposit that moved those pools let the attacker mint shares cheaply and redeem them at the restored price.

sources.ref: onchain review on Fantom over a public RPC: the PoC carries no transaction hash, so the exploit tx was recovered by querying eth_getLogs on the vault 0x4e332D616b5bA1eDFd87c899E534D996c336a2FC across the PoC's fork block window (34041497-34041503), which yields exactly one transaction, 0xca8dd338...0145 at block 34041500. Creation resolved by binary search over eth_getCode to block 23872504, 2021-12-03T12:34:32Z, creator 0x94c1deb52be70d6f281e6cdf2cd99c9e839808c4, not the attack-tx sender 0x12efed3512ea7b76f79bcde4a387216c7bce905e. Five EIP-1967 Upgraded events; the last is at block 33628407, 2022-03-17T03:01:55Z, installing 0xc06826f52f29b34c5d8b2c61abf844cebcf78abf, so the executing code was 4.65 days old. Loss $1.45 million per the DeFiHackLabs 2022 index entry for this PoC.
